message.content:
Below is a concise summary (in plain text) of key protections and responsibilities you have under Texas landlord‑tenant law. This is **general information only**—not tailored legal counsel—and may not cover all situations. If your circumstances differ or you face a dispute, consult a licensed attorney who practices in Texas. --- ### 1️⃣ Security Deposit Rules | Issue | What You Should Know | |-------|----------------------| | **Maximum amount** | Landlord may charge up to *one month*’s rent for residential units; no limit for commercial properties. | | **Return timeline** | Must return deposit within **30 days** after lease ends unless there are deductions. | | **Deductions allowed** | Unpaid rent, damage beyond normal wear & tear, cleaning costs if unit isn’t left clean, replacement of lost keys/locks. | | **Itemized statement** | Landlord must send written itemization of any deductions within those 30 days. | > ⚠️If the landlord fails to follow this schedule, they could lose the right to keep any portion of the security deposit. --- ### 2️⃣ Habitability / Repairs | Requirement | Your Rights | |-------------|--------------| | **Maintenance obligations** | Landlords must maintain plumbing, heating, electrical systems, structural integrity, pest control, etc., so the premises remain safe and livable. | | **Repair notice** | Tenants must notify landlords promptly (usually in writing). Failure to do so might waive certain claims. | | **Right to repair & deduct** | In some cases, tenants may fix minor repairs themselves and deduct reasonable cost from rent—but check local rules first. | | **Rent withholding** | Under Texas Property Code §92.006, you may legally refuse to pay rent until major habitability issues are fixed. However, you still owe “reasonable” rent while waiting. | --- ### 3️⃣ Lease Termination & Eviction Process | Stage | Key Points | |--------|------------| | **Notice requirements** | • For non‑renewal: at least **60 days** before end of lease.
• For termination due to breach: typically **10–15 day** notice depending on issue. | | **Eviction procedure** | Landlord must file a lawsuit → court summons → hearing → judgment → sheriff execution. No “self‑help” evictions (e.g., lock change without court order). | | **Tenant remedies** | File a counterclaim for unlawful eviction, seek damages, request injunction against illegal entry. | --- ### 4️⃣ Privacy & Entry Rights | Situation | Landlord's Right | |-----------|------------------| | **Routine inspections** | May enter with **24 hours' written notice**, except emergencies where immediate access is justified. | | **Emergency work** | Can enter without prior notice when necessary to prevent serious injury or property loss. | | **Personal belongings** | Landlord cannot remove them unless authorized by law or agreement. | --- ### 5️⃣ Discrimination Protections Under federal Fair Housing Act and Texas statutes: - Discriminatory actions based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, source of income, marital status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, or veteran status are prohibited. - Landlords cannot impose different terms solely because of protected characteristics. --- ### 6️⃣ Rental Payment & Late Fees | Rule | Details | |------|---------| | **Late fee limits** | Generally capped at **$50 per late payment** or **0.25% of monthly rent** (whichever is higher), whichever is less. | | **Grace period** | Many leases include a grace period (often 5–7 days); otherwise, rent becomes delinquent immediately. | | **Payment methods** | Landlords may accept checks, money orders, electronic transfers, etc.; they can't demand cash-only payments if other options exist. | --- ### 7️⃣ Move‑In Inspection Checklist Before moving out: - Document condition via photos/videos. - Keep receipts for any repairs you performed yourself. - Provide written move-out notice according to lease term (typically 30 days). These records help defend against unjustified deductions from your security deposit. --- #### Quick Reference Links - [Texas Property Code – Security Deposits](https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/?link=TXPCT) - [Texas Attorney General – Tenant Resources](https://www.txaag.org/TenantResources.aspx) --- **Disclaimer:** Laws evolve, and individual contracts may contain clauses that modify standard statutory rights. Always review your own lease carefully and consider seeking personalized guidance from a qualified Texas attorney if you encounter disputes or complex questions.
